# Medical Doctor It's time to heal. Or at least, try to heal, anyway. Medical Doctors are the primary caretakers of every boo boo and ouchie crewmembers get on the station, be it a small scratch, or boiled skin.
This guide will give you a basic outline of the treatment options you have available, triage, and other avenues of care.
## The Basics There are two ways to tell what's ailing someone: Taking a scan (with a health analyzer or a medical PDA), or examining them, with a shift-click, and clicking the heart symbol.
Using a health analyzer is often more powerful than examination, as some things (such as poison, or radiation) don't show up on examination. However, using an analyzer has its drawbacks, as it makes noise and takes up bag space.
## Medication and Treatment Options Before we go any further, it's probably a good idea to go over damage types, and what will heal them.
An important note: Most medication has an overdose level, which will cause harm to your patient. Chemicals also take time to metabolise, make sure not to inject too much too quickly.
- Brute Damage: Chemicals like Bicardine, brutepacks or surgery. - Burn Damage: Chemicals like Dermaline, ointment or surgery. - Toxin (Poison): Chemicals like Dylovene or surgery. - Toxin (Radiation) Chemicals like Arithrazine or surgery. - Asphyxiation: chemicals like Dexalin or defibrillators. - Bloodloss: chemicals like Saline or bloodpacks. - Bleeding: chemicals like Inaprovaline, gauze or cauterizing the wound with heat damage. - Genetic: chemicals like Phalanxamine or surgery.
Many stations are stocked with kits in storage, and all medics have some equipment in their starting belt.
## Basic Treatment and Triage Examine your patient, and note down the important details: Are they alive? Bleeding? What type of damage?
If alive, treat them as best as you can. Patients generaly are in critical condition at 100 damage, and dead at 200. Keep this in mind when choosing how to treat them. Emergency Pens and Epinephrine are often used to keep patients stable.
If possible, buckle them to a medical bed, if they are dead, strap them to a stasis bed or put them inside a body bag instead. Just keep in mind that metabolism (and by extension, healing chemicals) are slowed to a crawl when on stasis, they'll need to be taken off of it for the medicine to be effective.
## Assessing Corpses You can't save them all, sometimes, death happens. Depending on the [color=#a4885c]status[/color] of the body, there are a few things that can be done.
1. Do they have a soul attached? You can tell if, when examining, the following phrase is displayed: "Their soul has departed." If this isn't displayed, there is still a player who can be revived.
2. Is the body rotting? If it is, sadly, they'll require extensive surgery to reverse it or cloning. A rotting body can't be brought back with a defibrillator.
3. If they have a soul, it's possible to revive them. Consider storing the body in a morgue tray or body bag if you don't have enough time to revive someone, as the body will rot if you wait too long.
4. How damaged are they? If the body is above 400 total damage, they will require cryogenic treatment or surgery to bring back.
## Revival Not counting asphyxiation, Defibrillator's can be used to revive patients under 200 total damage. Chemicals don't metabolise in the dead, but all other methods can still patch them up. Use them to bring their numbers down enough for revival. Make sure the body will not rot during treatment, this can be done by strapping them to a stasis bed or surgical table. If the body's total damage is below 400, topicals (ointment, gauze, brutepacks, bloodpacks and automenders) can be applied to bring them below the revival treshold. If the body's damage is above 400, cryogenic treatment or surgery must be used.
Important note - some species will die at different damage amounts, if the defibrillator fails despite the patient being below 200 damage, try healing them more before trying again.
